review_brief:
# Review: 01f4294de005

## Built

The canonical sampler was repaired so row 1 is no longer globally excluded,
scalar/override types are strict, public axes have honest keyed provenance, the
redundant texture axis is gone, and feasible dense requests use whole-scene
placement retries instead of silently shrinking or failing because of greedy
order.

The native family adds `echo_mode=matching_marker` beside the byte-exact
canonical `none` rule.  Stage A maps orange-component area to a legend color.
Stage B uses that produced color to select the unique singleton marker and echo
the normalized component there.  Inputs are setting-neutral; 2–6 demonstrations
and four distinct queries are supported, including a substantive 30x30 query.

## Attempts to break it

The first versions failed real attacks: a disconnected size-6 sample, a
bounding-box-area shortcut, weak source-position crossing, Boolean-cell equality,
loose scalar contracts, a dead/redundant texture axis, mislabeled decoy draws, and
a feasible small-canvas placement failure.  Each cause was repaired and retained
as tests or in `adversarial_probe.py`.

On final bytes, 128 seeds produced 256 minimum lessons and 1,536 labelled pairs.
None of ten tested no-echo, geometric-proxy, rank, palette, or marker shortcuts
fit every demonstration.  The sweep also ran 18 protected-Racket jobs / 204
evaluations.  Native defect and override lint passed; the final authoring
preflight ran 32 additional protected-Racket evaluations.  A source-bound
wrong-intermediate witness changed 10 output cells.  Four exported episodes
produced 16 single-query views; 24 first-turn invariance checks, four positive
controls, and a deliberate private-answer injection rejection passed.

## Limits

These are finite reviewer checks, not a proof that no untested shortcut exists.
The causal interpretation remains an authored argument.  Owner qualification,
protected witness replay on integrated bytes, exact-source acceptance, and
training admission are still pending and were not claimed or enabled.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: For every orange component, the legend color selected by its measured area.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Measure each orange body component by cell area and use that 1-based area to select a color from the ordered top-row legend.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Use the selected legend color to locate its unique singleton body marker, recolor the source component, and echo the component normalized at that marker.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The destination marker is identified by the color produced in step A; before that color exists, step B cannot choose which singleton marker receives the shape. Replacing the area-derived colors changes both source recoloring and echo destinations.
